questions.question: Which of the following products or activities is explicitly outside the scope of TR60?

options.A: Processes for biological/biotechnology products such as vaccines, blood-derived products and ATMPs
options.B: Processes for sterile and non-sterile drugs, and for radiopharmaceuticals and veterinary drugs
options.C: Manufacture of medical devices (unless part of a combination product) and dietary supplements
options.D: Processes for the drug constituent and active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) of combination products (drug plus device)

questions.explanation: TR60 applies to drug substances and drug products, including sterile and non-sterile drugs, biologics, APIs, radiopharmaceuticals, veterinary drugs and the drug constituent of combination products; explicitly excluded are medical devices (except as part of combination products), dietary supplements, medicated feed and human tissue (except tissue engineering in ATMPs).

questions.question: How does TR60 distinguish continued process verification from continuous process verification?

options.A: The former is an FDA term for activities that keep a process in a state of control, covering all manufacturing scenarios; the latter refers to process verification using advanced technologies such as PAT
options.B: The former refers specifically to process verification using advanced manufacturing and analytical technologies such as PAT; the latter is an FDA term for all activities that maintain a state of control
options.C: They are the same concept, with FDA and EMA simply using different names, and the two can be used interchangeably in TR60
options.D: The former applies only to annual review of traditional batch processes; the latter applies only to processes approved for real-time release

questions.explanation: TR60 states explicitly that the two have different meanings: continuous refers to process verification using advanced technologies such as PAT, while continued is an FDA term covering all manufacturing scenarios, whether traditional, advanced technology or a hybrid of both. The option saying the former is PAT process verification and the latter an FDA term simply reverses the two, and "the same concept" and "annual review / real-time release only" are not how the document puts it.

questions.question: According to the TR60 Glossary, what is the relationship between the Normal Operating Range (NOR) and the Proven Acceptable Range (PAR)?

options.A: The NOR encompasses the whole PAR and extends beyond it; the PAR is a narrower range selected within the NOR
options.B: The NOR and PAR are the same range, called the PAR in Stage 1 and renamed the NOR in the commercial production stage
options.C: The NOR is determined by the regulator-approved design space, while the PAR is set by the manufacturing site itself
options.D: The NOR is the control target and range of a process parameter, specified in the manufacturing instructions, that lies within the PAR

questions.explanation: The Glossary defines the NOR as the target and range of control of a parameter, specified in the manufacturing instructions and lying within the PAR, within which manufacture yields material or product that meets release criteria and CQAs. The option saying the NOR encompasses the whole PAR reverses the containment, and "the same range" and "the NOR is determined by the design space" are not the definitions in the document.

questions.question: A process parameter has no effect on quality at its own step, but going outside its range could affect the performance of the next process step. According to the TR60 Glossary, how should the parameter be classified?

options.A: Critical Process Parameter (CPP), because any parameter that affects the process must be controlled
options.B: Noncritical process parameter, which may be monitored for process control purposes
options.C: Critical Quality Attribute (CQA), because it ultimately affects the quality of the finished product
options.D: Quality attribute, because it is a product characteristic that can serve as a release specification

questions.explanation: A CPP is defined as one whose variability affects a CQA; a parameter with no impact on quality at that step is a noncritical parameter, and the document specifically notes that it may affect the performance of the next step, so it may be monitored for process control purposes. CQAs and quality attributes are product attributes, not process parameters that can be directly controlled.

questions.topic: GMP and documentation across the lifecycle
questions.question: What does TR60 say about GMP and documentation requirements across the lifecycle stages?

options.A: Not all lifecycle activities must be performed under GMP (for example, some Stage 1 studies), and documentation requirements are highest in the process qualification and validation stages
options.B: Studies in all three stages must be performed under GMP, and documentation requirements are exactly the same in every stage
options.C: Only Stage 3 needs quality unit approval; Stages 1 and 2 are the responsibility of the R&D department alone, with no quality involvement needed
options.D: Documentation requirements are highest in Stage 1, because process design documentation must be progressively reduced in later stages, with the PPQ stage needing only brief records

questions.explanation: TR60 notes that some Stage 1 process design studies need not be performed under GMP, although the involvement of quality and regulatory representatives is still recommended; documentation requirements are greatest in the process qualification and validation stages, whose studies must comply with GMP and be approved by the quality unit.

questions.question: According to TR60, when should the QTPP (Quality Target Product Profile) be established?

options.A: After PPQ is completed, compiling the quality characteristics the product should have from the PPQ results
options.B: At the start of Stage 1, and referred to continuously throughout the product lifecycle
options.C: Only before Stage 2 starts, working backward from the established CQAs to the overall product quality targets
options.D: At the time of the marketing authorisation application, the first time the product's quality targets are documented

questions.explanation: Per ICH Q8(R2), the QTPP is a prospective summary of the quality characteristics of a drug product that ideally will be achieved; it is decided at the very start of Stage 1 and referred to throughout the lifecycle. CQAs are derived from the QTPP, not the other way around.

questions.question: According to TR60, what is the main basis for judging how critical a quality attribute is?

options.A: The attribute's potential impact on safety and efficacy (the severity of harm), assessed with ICH Q9(R1) risk tools
options.B: Whether the attribute is already in the release specification; every attribute in the specification is treated as critical, and any not in it is disregarded
options.C: Whether the test method for the attribute is expensive or time-consuming; the greater the testing burden, the more critical, ranked by testing cost
options.D: The size of the variability in the attribute's values in early development batches; the greater the variability, the sooner it is treated as critical, regardless of severity of harm

questions.explanation: The criticality of a CQA should be based on risk tools, taking into account the severity of harm, that is, the potential impact on safety and efficacy. The release specification measures only a selected subset of quality attributes, and the document also notes that some characteristics are not in release testing, so "everything in the release specification is critical" does not hold; testing cost and early-batch variability are not bases listed in the document.

questions.question: Robustness studies in process characterization show that a parameter originally classified as a CPP can vary widely without affecting the CQAs. How does TR60 recommend handling this?

options.A: Keep the CPP classification unchanged, and review the classification of this parameter only after PPQ is complete
options.B: Remove the parameter from the control strategy entirely, no longer monitoring or recording it at any step
options.C: Re-evaluate the classification of the parameter through a subsequent risk assessment, with the conclusion supported by data
options.D: Downgrade the affected CQA to an ordinary quality attribute, because the parameter itself is still a CPP

questions.explanation: The document notes that a parameter may initially be classified as a CPP, but when robustness data from process characterization show that CQAs are not affected, the role of the subsequent risk assessment is to re-evaluate the classification; decision trees can also be used for iterative risk assessment before and after characterization studies.

questions.question: If conclusions from laboratory-scale studies are to be applied directly to the commercial-scale process, what does TR60 require of the scale-down model?

options.A: As long as equipment of the same make as at commercial scale is used, no process data need be compared and no correction of predicted values is needed
options.B: As long as the facility and utility qualification reports are provided, the model is considered qualified, with no need to compare process outputs
options.C: Compensate by increasing the number of PPQ batches, so the model itself need not be qualified in advance and quality attributes need not be compared
options.D: The model must be confirmed as representative of the full-scale process, by comparing process parameters, inputs and outputs, including product quality attributes

questions.explanation: Qualification of a scale-down model must show that its performance is representative of the full-scale process, which is done by comparing process parameters and inputs/outputs (including product quality attributes); where the model and predictions differ, appropriate corrections should be made. Equipment make, facility reports or additional PPQ batches cannot replace this qualification.

questions.question: According to TR60, what is the main benefit of using a PACMP (post-approval change management protocol, also called a comparability protocol)?

options.A: It can replace the in-house change control procedure, so no filing with the regulator is needed for changes
options.B: It lets all post-approval changes be classified in the lowest risk category, to be submitted only in the annual report
options.C: It removes the legally binding status of established conditions, so the firm can adjust them flexibly
options.D: For anticipated changes, a lower reporting category can be used, and the timelines for review and implementation are accelerated

questions.explanation: A PACMP specifies in advance the anticipated changes, the method of assessment, the acceptance criteria to be met and the proposed reporting category; with a robust verification and testing strategy, it can lower the reporting category and shorten review and implementation time. It does not replace change control, nor does it make established conditions lose their force.

questions.question: What is TR60's view on the number of successful PPQ batches?

options.A: Regulations state explicitly that at least three consecutive successful batches are needed to complete PPQ, so the number of batches is the main goal of PPQ
options.B: The more batches the better; adding batches can make up for gaps in the control strategy, regardless of risk and level of knowledge
options.C: The number of batches is not the main goal of PPQ; the batches are used to collect the data needed to show that the control strategy is effective
options.D: One successful commercial-scale batch is enough to demonstrate the process design and release for marketing, with no other batches needed

questions.explanation: TR60 stresses that the number of successful PPQ batches should not be treated as the main goal; the batches are a means of collecting data that demonstrate the effectiveness of the control strategy. Neither regulators nor industry set a fixed number of batches, and the number should be determined by risk and statistical justification.

questions.question: A new formulation with new equipment has a very low level of process knowledge. According to the risk assessment table in TR60, how should PPQ be planned?

options.A: Run PPQ directly with N = Baseline batches, with no additional development or preparatory work and no leadership approval needed
options.B: Treat it as high risk, first consider additional development or preparatory activities, and proceed to PPQ only after leadership approval with the risks detailed
options.C: Treat it as low risk, with the number of batches allowed to be below Baseline, to save cost for the first commercial manufacture and shorten time to market
options.D: Level of knowledge does not affect the number of batches; always use the three batches of EU Annex 15 as the final number, with no further risk assessment

questions.explanation: In Table 4.4.2.2-1, a low level of knowledge corresponds to high risk, and it is recommended to consider additional development or preparatory activities and to begin PPQ only after leadership approval with the risks detailed; N = Baseline applies to a typical level of knowledge, and N <= Baseline to a high level of knowledge. The three batches of Annex 15 are only a starting point for the assessment.

questions.question: The same drug solution is to be filled into vials of different volumes, with only the container size changing and other variables fixed, and the company plans to run PPQ on only the smallest and largest sizes. What approach is this?

options.A: Bracketing, in which the extremes of a process variable represent the intermediate sizes in between, and scientific and risk-based justification is required
options.B: Matrix, because one batch must be made for every combination of each volume with the other variables, and no risk assessment is needed
options.C: Family, because the sizes are treated as a group of related but essentially different entities from which representatives are selected, without involving extremes
options.D: Concurrent validation, because commercial batches are released before PPQ is complete, which has nothing to do with selecting sizes

questions.explanation: Bracketing is used when a single process element varies and other variables are fixed, for example different container sizes or fill volumes within the same container closure system, with the extremes representing the intermediate group; the rationale for the selection must be scientifically supported and risk assessed, and written into the PVMP and PPQ protocol. A matrix approach is used for combinations of more than one variable.

questions.question: If PPQ uses an approach of individual unit operation studies, what does TR60 recommend for reporting?

options.A: Only one overall process report is needed, with the results of each unit operation covered by a one-sentence summary and no separate reports
options.B: Each unit operation produces its own report, but no overall conclusion for the whole process is needed because each has already met its acceptance criteria
options.C: Wait until enough data have accumulated in Stage 3, then compile the results of all unit operations into a report, with no report in the PPQ stage
options.D: Write a separate report for each unit operation, plus a summary report that consolidates all results to support PPQ of the overall process

questions.explanation: With the unit operation approach, a PPQ report is prepared for each unit operation study, and a summary executive report is written separately, consolidating the results of all studies to support PPQ of the entire process; each report should also state pass or fail against every acceptance criterion.

questions.question: A unit operation yields a homogeneous pool of bulk solution, and multiple samples are taken from that pool for testing. What does TR60 say about the meaning of this and the alternative approach?

options.A: It reflects within-batch variability of the process, so the more samples the greater the statistical confidence, with no need to compare data between batches
options.B: It can only show that test results pass, with no need to compare data on intermediate pools between batches or to do extended characterization
options.C: It reflects only the variability of the analytical method rather than within-batch process variability, and extended characterization of the intermediate pool with comparison of data between batches can be used instead
options.D: It represents the worst case for the whole batch, so sampling at other locations and batch-to-batch comparison can be waived, with no extended characterization needed

questions.explanation: Repeated sampling of a single homogeneous pool gives only the variability of the analytical method, not within-batch process variability, and a statistical sampling plan is of limited use here; the document recommends extended characterization of the intermediate pool, non-routine sampling at specific points in the process, and comparison of data between batches to show process control and reproducibility.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of Stage 3a in TR60?

options.A: To validate the commercial process in place of PPQ, so that Stage 2 can be omitted
options.B: To be started only when a change occurs, replacing routine Stage 3b monitoring
options.C: To fold in the content of the annual product quality review (APQR) as the entire content of the CPV program
options.D: To establish a data baseline with enhanced sampling and confirm the subsequent Stage 3b monitoring plan

questions.explanation: Stage 3a is a protocol-based initial evaluation after launch of a new product, using enhanced sampling and testing, with the purpose of understanding variability and establishing the baseline and limits for Stage 3b; confirming the Stage 3b monitoring plan is part of Stage 3a. It does not replace PPQ, and it is not only for when changes occur.

questions.question: What is TR60's view of the relationship between CPV and the annual product quality review (APQR)?

options.A: Having an APQR is enough to replace CPV, because both review process data annually, with identical content and frequency
options.B: A summary of CPV data can be used in the relevant APQR sections, but the APQR cannot replace CPV, and CAPA should not wait for the APQR
options.C: CPV is compiled only once at the time of the APQR; per-batch monitoring is extra work rather than part of CPV, and no CAPA is needed
options.D: CPV results may not be cited in the APQR; the two must be completely independent to avoid duplicated data, with CAPA deferred to the annual review

questions.explanation: TR60 states explicitly that the APQR should not be used to replace CPV; ongoing monitoring and CAPA should be carried out for every batch and should not be postponed until the APQR, but a summary of CPV data should be used in or referenced by the relevant APQR sections, and Stage 3b covers much of the APQR content.

questions.question: When many sensitizing rules are added to a Shewhart chart to detect trends earlier, what risk does TR60 warn about?

options.A: The rate of false alarms rises significantly, so the number of rules should be kept reasonable
options.B: The control limits automatically widen, making real process shifts harder to detect, so the more rules the less sensitive the chart
options.C: The control chart changes from a variables chart into an attributes chart, the baseline must be rebuilt, and all historical data become invalid
options.D: The required sample size is automatically halved, so the sampling frequency is insufficient to support statistical decisions, and the control limits also become invalid

questions.explanation: Sensitizing rules can detect drifts, shifts or changes in variability earlier, but the more rules are added, the higher the proportion of false alarms, so the document recommends keeping the number of rules reasonable. The other options are not consequences of adding rules.

questions.question: What is TR60's principle for handling CPV signals?

options.A: Treat any signal as OOS, immediately start batch rejection and a full investigation, regardless of statistical significance or level of risk
options.B: All signals are equally important, and a single fixed action plan is applied to all of them, with no assessment of risk or cause
options.C: Classify signals by risk, and after assessing whether the cause is common cause, special cause or assignable cause, decide between continued monitoring, evaluating the control strategy or a change, to avoid overreaction
options.D: Act only on CQA signals; signals on CPPs and material attributes are left for the annual review, with no separate investigation or tracking

questions.explanation: CPV signals are like "yellow flags": not every signal is equally important, so they should be classified on a risk basis (for example, CPPs, CQAs) and evaluated case by case; after it is confirmed that the signal is not an OOS/OOT/deviation, its statistical significance is evaluated and its cause determined to decide the next path, with the aim of avoiding overreaction as well as failing to act when action is needed.

questions.question: What approach does TR60 recommend for acquiring and managing CPV data?

options.A: Data should be transcribed manually as far as possible and then entered centrally, so that every data point is checked by a person
options.B: Acquire and parse data automatically directly from instruments, with robust data governance and DI controls
options.C: Each department maintains its own data in an independent format, avoiding centralized management and the security risk it creates
options.D: No specific format is required when data are acquired, with data tidied into a statistical format at the annual review

questions.explanation: TR60 recommends acquiring and parsing data automatically and directly from instruments wherever possible, with robust data governance and data integrity (DI) controls, ensuring consistency and alignment with industry-standard ontologies and taxonomies; data should be in a format suitable for statistical analysis to support CPV and APQR/YBPR.

questions.question: Which of the following is a risk management application listed in TR60 as belonging to Stage 2 (process qualification)?

options.A: Performing a preliminary criticality (severity) analysis of the product's CQAs and deciding their priority in process design
options.B: Deciding which parameters CPV will monitor and the duration of enhanced sampling, and setting the control chart rules
options.C: Deciding which process steps and parameters PPQ will test, including the sampling plan with its confidence and coverage
options.D: Using preliminary hazard analysis or early FMEA to screen the potential variables to enter process characterization, and planning the DoE scope

questions.explanation: QRM in Stage 2 includes deciding the steps and parameters to be tested in PPQ (including the confidence and coverage of the sampling plan), impact assessment of facility and equipment systems, acceptance criteria for each test function, and analytical results and deviations. "Preliminary CQA criticality analysis" and "screening process characterization variables with early FMEA" belong to Stage 1, and "deciding CPV monitoring parameters" belongs to Stage 3.

questions.question: According to TR60, what is the main reason DoE is better than the traditional "one factor at a time" approach?

options.A: DoE needs very few experiments, so no statistical software or model is needed, and interactions need not be analyzed
options.B: DoE can directly replace PPQ, so no commercial-scale batches need be run in Stage 2 and no report is needed
options.C: DoE is used only for trend monitoring in Stage 3, while one factor at a time can be used only for early screening in Stage 1
options.D: DoE can identify interactions between parameters, whereas one factor at a time cannot show whether the effect of one parameter changes with the levels of the others

questions.explanation: Changing one parameter at a time with the others held fixed cannot reveal parameter interactions, that is, where the effect of one parameter on a quality attribute differs with the levels of other parameters; DoE is often used in Stage 1 to identify significant input parameters and establish the design space, and confirmation experiments can sometimes make use of Stage 2 results.

questions.question: To evaluate process capability using a "long-term" standard deviation that includes between-batch variation, which set of indices should be used?

options.A: Pp and PpK, because a standard deviation calculated from all data pooled together includes between-batch and other between-group variation
options.B: Cp and CpK, because their standard deviation is estimated from within-subgroup variation on the control chart and covers between-batch variation
options.C: Cp only, because when the process is centered it already reflects the overall variation both within and between batches
options.D: The OC curve, because it describes the probability of acceptance and directly gives the value of the process capability index

questions.explanation: A standard deviation estimated from a control chart excludes variation in the means between groups (such as between batches) and is used for Cp and CpK; if the standard deviation is calculated from all the data pooled, it includes between-batch variation, and the indices are then called Pp and PpK. When the process is not in control, Pp and PpK are more appropriate, although this approach is somewhat debated.

questions.topic: Confidence in acceptance sampling for PPQ
questions.question: When prior confidence is low and statistical acceptance sampling is used to support PPQ, what minimum confidence level does TR60 recommend, and what does it mean?

options.A: At least 95% confidence, corresponding to the Type I error of wrongly rejecting an acceptable lot, exactly the same as the confidence concept of the AQL
options.B: At least 90% confidence, corresponding to the Type II error of wrongly accepting an unacceptable process, which differs from the 95% of the AQL
options.C: At least 80% confidence, because PPQ has few batches and it is usually unrealistic to expect a higher statistical confidence level
options.D: At least 99% confidence, which is enough to cover the three different sampling concepts, RQL, LTPD and AQL, and their errors

questions.explanation: TR60 recommends that when prior confidence is not high, at least 90% confidence be achieved at the end of PPQ; this is the traditional confidence for detecting an unacceptable quality level (RQL/LTPD) and concerns the Type II error, which differs from the 95% acceptance confidence (Type I error) associated with the AQL.

questions.question: A product is already marketed and in commercial production, and is now to be transferred to another manufacturing site. According to TR60, at which stage does this kind of technology transfer usually occur?

options.A: Stage 3 (or between Stage 2 and Stage 3), because the product is already in commercial manufacturing
options.B: Before Stage 1, because any transfer must be completed before process design begins and may not be made afterwards
options.C: Between Stage 1 and Stage 2, because this is the only time at which a transfer from R&D to commercial manufacturing occurs
options.D: Only during PPQ execution, because the transfer must be completed simultaneously with process qualification, without exception

questions.explanation: TR60 explains that when a new process moves from development to commercial manufacturing, technology transfer usually occurs between Stage 1 and Stage 2; if the product is already marketed, the transfer generally occurs in Stage 3 (or ultimately between Stage 2 and Stage 3). The criterion for a successful TT is that the receiving unit can demonstrate consistent manufacture through process verification.

questions.question: Section 7.0 of TR60 uses equipment maintenance as an example to show the importance of knowledge management (KM) to risk assessment. If there are gaps in information or data (whether tacit or explicit), what is the consequence?

options.A: The risk assessment is still robust, but more time is needed to collect and organize data
options.B: It directly leads to a less robust risk assessment, increasing product quality risk and possibly affecting patient safety
options.C: It affects only trend analysis in Stage 3 and has no effect on risk assessment in Stage 1
options.D: It affects only the completeness of the documentation system and does not affect the assessment of quality risk or later decisions

questions.explanation: The document states that a sound risk assessment requires a complete and well-managed KM system; gaps in information and data (tacit or explicit) directly make the risk assessment less robust, increase product quality risk, and may affect patient safety; the related assessment and mitigation plans are incorporated at the design level in Stage 1.

questions.question: In process characterization for the large molecule (humanized IgG1) example, the downstream process was found to have acidic variants that affect biological activity. How did the team respond?

options.A: Relax the upper load limit of the Protein A column to reduce the proportion of acidic variants
options.B: Test for acidic variants only at release, with no further control at intermediate stages of the process
options.C: Move all the characterization studies to commercial scale and repeat them, abandoning the use of the scale-down model
options.D: Impose tighter control on in-process hold times, and update the quality risk assessment and control strategy

questions.explanation: In the example, process characterization found that acidic variants affect biological activity, so tighter in-process hold time controls were set to control the amount of acidic variants, and the QRA and control strategy were updated; the final drug substance concentration was also raised to save storage capacity.

questions.question: In the large molecule example, why was the frozen condition chosen at the start of formulation development, while a liquid formulation was developed in parallel?

options.A: The regulator requires biologics at the clinical stage always to be in frozen form
options.B: The liquid formulation was shown to be unable to meet stability requirements within 24 months
options.C: Because the frozen form is easier to control, while the liquid formulation was in parallel development
options.D: Because frozen packaging costs less, so frozen was used for both the clinical and commercial stages

questions.explanation: Table 7.1-1 explains that the frozen condition was chosen initially because it was easy to control, while a liquid formulation was developed in parallel; the final goal in the QTPP was a liquid formulation at 20 mg/mL with a shelf life of at least 24 months at 2-8 °C. The document does not mention the other options.

questions.question: In the large molecule example, how was the number of PPQ runs decided, and what was the result?

options.A: A qualitative decision tool combined factors such as process variability, raw material variability, equipment age and operator experience, and recommended 5-6 batches
options.B: Directly per EU Annex 15, a fixed three consecutive successful batches were used, with no other risk assessment
options.C: Using average run length (ARL), 22 consecutive conforming batches were calculated before PPQ could be completed and commercial release begin
options.D: It was determined by the bioreactor capacity, with 2000 L corresponding to a fixed number of PPQ batches, regardless of process risk

questions.explanation: The example used a qualitative decision tool that considered process variability (such as novel or difficult scale-up operations), raw material variability, age of equipment and facilities, operators' commercial manufacturing experience, clinical manufacturing experience and robustness of the control strategy, and recommended 5-6 PPQ batches; the first PPQ batch was at full scale and the later batches at about 10% scale.

questions.question: In the large molecule example, what was done in the engineering runs performed at technology transfer, and what additional benefit did they bring?

options.A: They used non-GMP substitute materials and approved formal batch records, with the purpose only of testing equipment performance, and no operator training was involved
options.B: Three commercial release batches were made, and the data obtained replaced the requirement for the number of PPQ batches, with no draft records needed
options.C: Two runs were made with GMP materials and draft batch production records to fine-tune set points, and the operators were also trained
options.D: Only one small-scale laboratory trial was done, to confirm that the quality unit had completed all approvals, with no set points involved

questions.explanation: In the example, two engineering runs (GMP materials, draft batch production records) demonstrated that the process was feasible and fine-tuned the operating set points, and also trained operators on the new process; the Process Design Summary Report was later updated for changes to process parameters.

questions.question: In the large molecule CPV example (Table 7.1-3), how were the control limits established in stages?

options.A: Preliminary limits after 3 batches and final limits after 10 batches, with no further updating of limits afterwards
options.B: Preliminary limits after 5 batches and final limits after 20 batches, with no further updating of limits afterwards
options.C: Preliminary limits after 20 batches and final limits after 50 batches, with no further updating of limits afterwards
options.D: Preliminary limits after 15 commercial batches (including PPQ batches) and final limits after 30 batches

questions.explanation: In the example, preliminary control limits were established after 15 commercial batches (including PPQ batches) were completed, and final control limits after 30 commercial batches; the CPV plan was drawn up and submitted to the regulator before PPQ began.

questions.question: Which statement about the composition and responsibilities of the Product Technical Team (PTT) in the example is correct?

options.A: It consists only of the quality department, dedicated to approving batch release and directly making all process change decisions
options.B: It is a cross-functional team, including manufacturing, process development, MSAT, analytical, quality and statistics, which reviews the data accumulated in commercial production and can recommend process changes
options.C: It consists only of regulatory affairs and supply chain staff, responsible for managing the marketing authorisation and the raw material supply to each site
options.D: It consists of external consultants, who review once only before the product launch and then disband to avoid conflicts of interest

questions.explanation: In the example, a PTT is set up for each commercial product to oversee the process for the rest of its lifecycle; it is a cross-functional team that reviews the data accumulated in commercial production, can recommend process changes and help with continuous improvement, and also reviews data from multiple manufacturing sites to ensure consistent process performance and product quality.

questions.question: In the small molecule injectable example, what led the team to decide on aseptic manufacture rather than terminal sterilization?

options.A: DoE results showed that the drug product is heat sensitive and therefore unsuitable for terminal sterilization
options.B: The regulator requires all solution dosage forms to be made by aseptic processing
options.C: PPQ results showed that the failure rate of aseptic filling is lower than that of terminal sterilization
options.D: Differences between the specifications of the three concentrations meant the terminal sterilization equipment could not handle them all

questions.explanation: Table 7.2-1 explains that the DoE concluded that the DP is heat sensitive, so aseptic manufacture was adopted instead of terminal sterilization; subsequent pilot batches went on to study the effect of the highest solution temperature during mixing, filtration and filling on degradation rate and impurities.

questions.topic: Table 7.2-3 - Statistical tools by data volume
questions.question: In the small molecule CPV example, when are process-robustness contour plots used, and when are PpK/CpK used?

options.A: Contour plots when there are many data points (25 or more), and PpK/CpK only when there are few data points
options.B: Both can be used only when there are more than 100 data points, and no statistics are done with less data
options.C: Contour plots when there are few data points (for example, fewer than 20-25), and PpK and/or CpK when there are 25 or more
options.D: Contour plots are used only for PPQ, and PpK/CpK only for deviation investigations

questions.explanation: The example states that process-robustness contour plots are used when there are few data points (for example, fewer than 20-25), and process performance capability indices such as PpK and/or CpK when there are 25 or more data points. The other statements are not in the document.

questions.question: How were the Process Evaluation (PE) batches of the small molecule example designed?

options.A: Two 400 L pilot-scale batches, using API from the same supplier, run at the lowest-concentration specification
options.B: Three commercial release batches, using API from three suppliers, performed entirely independently by site manufacturing personnel
options.C: One small-scale batch at the lowest concentration, operated under standard conditions, with no extended in-process controls
options.D: Two full-scale batches, using the highest DP concentration and API from two different suppliers, with bracketing and extended in-process controls

questions.explanation: Table 7.2-1 describes the PE study as performed before the stability batches using bracketing: two scale-up batches at the highest DP concentration, with API from two different suppliers, both at full scale (2800 L), based on the risk assessment and accompanied by an extended in-process control plan, and demonstrating compliance with the finished product specification under worst-case conditions.

questions.topic: Average run length to detect failure rate
questions.question: Under the ARL method in the appendix (ARL = 1/p), if a batch failure rate of 10% is considered unacceptable, on average how many batches are needed before the first batch failure is detected?

options.A: About 5 batches, because ARL is proportional to the failure rate
options.B: About 10 batches, because 1/0.1 = 10
options.C: About 20 batches, because the failure rate must be doubled before calculating
options.D: About 100 batches, because ARL is the failure rate multiplied by 1000 and rounded

questions.explanation: ARL = 1/p: with a batch failure rate p = 0.10, a failure is detected on average once every 1/0.1 = 10 batches; the example in the document is that a 20% failure rate is detected on average once every 5 batches. The value of p is often chosen as 25%, 20%, 10% or 5%, with 5% usually the strictest.

questions.question: If the PPQ acceptance criterion is to demonstrate, with 90% confidence, a lot conformance rate of at least 90%, how many consecutive conforming batches are needed? If 50% confidence is used instead, how many batches does the PPQ stage need?

options.A: 22 consecutive conforming batches are needed; with 50% confidence, 7 batches in PPQ suffice, with the remaining 15 made up in early CPV
options.B: 3 consecutive conforming batches are needed; with 50% confidence, only 1 batch in PPQ is needed, with the remaining batches made up in CPV
options.C: 10 consecutive conforming batches are needed; with 50% confidence, only 5 batches in PPQ are needed, with the remaining batches made up in CPV
options.D: 45 consecutive conforming batches are needed; with 50% confidence, only 22 batches in PPQ are needed, with the remaining batches made up in CPV

questions.explanation: In the example of Table 9.6-1, demonstrating a lot conformance rate of at least 90% with 90% confidence requires 22 consecutive conforming batches; after 7 batches passed, the rate is already "more likely than not" above 90% (50% confidence), PPQ can be considered complete, and the other 15 batches are made up in early CPV to reach 22.

questions.question: An active ingredient has an assay specification of 95-105, with one assay result per batch. Which statement is correct when the PRE-Control concept is applied to PPQ?

options.A: The narrow limits are 90-110; three consecutive batches within the narrow limits, and the narrow limits are also used to decide batch release
options.B: The narrow limits are 99-101; one batch within the narrow limits completes PPQ, and the narrow limits can replace the original specification
options.C: The narrow limits are 97.5-102.5; five consecutive batches within them complete PPQ, and the narrow limits are not used to judge batch acceptance
options.D: The narrow limits are 92.5-107.5; ten consecutive batches within them complete PPQ, and they must replace the original specification

questions.explanation: PRE-Control is a form of narrow-limit gauging, using the middle 50% of the specification range as the narrow limits; for an assay of 95-105 the narrow limits are 97.5-102.5, and five consecutive batches within the narrow limits complete PPQ. The narrow limits are used only to judge whether the PPQ acceptance criterion has been met, not for acceptance of batches.

questions.question: Instead of calculating a parametric confidence interval for PpK, an approach is used that requires consecutive batches each to meet the PpK acceptance criterion. What does TR60 say about the confidence this provides?

options.A: Two batches each with PpK >= 1.0 provide more than 90% confidence, and three batches more than 99%
options.B: Three batches each with PpK >= 1.0 provide more than 95% confidence, and four batches more than 99%
options.C: Six batches each with PpK >= 1.0 are needed to provide more than 90% confidence, and ten batches more than 95%
options.D: Four batches each with PpK >= 1.0 provide more than 90% confidence, and five batches more than 95%

questions.explanation: The document states that requiring four or five consecutive batches each to meet the PpK acceptance criterion is an alternative to calculating a parametric confidence interval: four batches each with PpK >= 1.0 provide more than 90% confidence that the process median PpK is >= 1.0, and five batches more than 95%.

questions.question: To monitor the number of cosmetic defects per 100 glass vials (count of defects, Poisson data), which control chart listed in the appendix is the most suitable?

options.A: A p-chart, used to record the proportion of defective units (binomial data)
options.B: A c-chart, used to record the number of defects (Poisson data)
options.C: An x-bar/R chart, used to track the mean and range of continuous measurements with +/-3 sigma limits
options.D: A CUSUM chart, used to accumulate the deviation of continuous measurements from the target

questions.explanation: Among control charts for attributes data, the c-chart is used for the number of defects (Poisson data); the p-chart and np-chart are used for the proportion or number of defectives (binomial). The x-bar/R and CUSUM charts are for variables data. The count of defects is exactly the example the document describes with the Poisson distribution.
